title: WP Sell Services - admin-ajax to wpss/v1 REST migration map
summary: Maps every frontend admin-ajax action to its wpss/v1 REST twin. As of 1.2.0 ALL flows (KG-1 through KG-7) are migrated and browser-verified - the HTML-rendering flows now use shared server-side renderers (wpss_render_services_grid, wpss_render_message_row) exposed over REST, and the vendor-profile twin was brought to full field+table parity (one canonical store). All legacy wp_ajax_* handlers remain registered as backward-compatible delegates - nothing was removed. former_blocker fields are retained as the historical record of what was resolved.
resolved_1_2_0: KG-1 reviews load-more, KG-2 review helpful, KG-3 services grid, KG-4 conversation send+poll (incl. multipart attachments), KG-5 vendor profile parity (intro video + table storage; also fixed the _wpss_is_vendor vs wpss_is_vendor() guard bug shared by both transports), KG-6 single-service favorites (dead handler removed; live toggle already REST), KG-7 delivery multipart upload.

conventions.js_client: jQuery $.ajax with beforeSend X-WP-Nonce (the established in-repo REST idiom; see assets/js/frontend.js favorites + reviews flows)
conventions.legacy_handlers: kept registered in src/Frontend/AjaxHandlers.php for backward compatibility; each already delegates to the same Service its REST twin uses

flows.name: favorites - toggle (single service page)
flows.former_blocker: Migration requires localizing apiUrl + restNonce onto the wpssService object, which lives in src/Frontend/SingleServiceView.php::enqueue_assets() - that file is OUTSIDE this direction's scope (scope allows only src/Frontend/AjaxHandlers.php under src/Frontend/). The dependent single-service.js change was reverted to avoid calling an undefined wpssService.apiUrl (which would break favorites). FavoritesController add_favorite/remove_favorite were still given an additive `count` field (in-scope, src/API/**) so the migration is a one-line localization away once SingleServiceView.php is in scope.

flows.name: favorites - toggle (services archive / cards)
flows.notes: Already migrated to REST before this wave (pre-existing); left unchanged. Proven reference pattern for this direction.

flows.name: favorites - remove from saved grid (unified dashboard)
flows.notes: Migrated to REST DELETE. Reads response.count (now returned by remove_favorite) to update the saved-count label. Uses the dashboard's existing restUrl + restNonce localized keys.

flows.name: service status toggle (pause / publish on dashboard)
flows.shared_backend: wp_update_post (both paths); REST restricts status to publish|draft (6.0b merged)
flows.notes: Migrated to PUT /services/{id} with explicit target status. The legacy AJAX flipped status server-side; the JS now flips client-side (currentStatus -> targetStatus) and reads response.status (= post_status) from the prepared service response. update_item_permissions_check enforces vendor ownership, matching the AJAX post_author check.

flows.name: order lifecycle transitions (accept/reject/start/deliver/complete/cancel/accept-cancellation/reject-cancellation)
flows.shared_service: WPSellServices\Services\OrderService (update_status / start_work / request_revision / cancel) - the SAME service both the AJAX handlers and the REST twin route through
flows.notes: Migrated to REST. The frontend consumer only needs success/failure (it does location.reload() on success and ignores the body), so the migration is byte-compatible from the consumer's perspective. Frontend action keys map 1:1 to the REST action regex segments. Legacy wp_ajax_* handlers remain as delegates to the same OrderService methods.

flows.name: reviews - load more (single service page)
flows.former_blocker: NOT byte-compatible. load_reviews returns ob_get_clean() server-rendered review HTML ({html, has_more}); the JS appends response.data.html directly. The REST GET /reviews returns a structured JSON list envelope, not HTML. Migrating requires client-side review rendering (a behavior/markup change) which violates direction 6.3.1's 'byte-compatible response shapes; nothing removed' constraint. frontend.js's reviews-load was migrated separately with bespoke client rendering; replicating that for single-service.js is a markup-parity rewrite that must be browser-verified, out of safe scope for this static pass.

flows.name: reviews - mark helpful (single service page)
flows.former_blocker: Adjacent to reviews-load; deferred with it to keep the single-service reviews block migrated as one verified unit rather than half-converted. Response shape ({count}) is compatible, but it shares the reviews block and should be browser-verified together.

flows.name: services - load / pagination (services block)
flows.former_blocker: NOT byte-compatible. load_services returns ob_get_clean() server-rendered cards HTML ({html, pagination}); the JS appends it to the grid. GET /services returns structured JSON. Same HTML-vs-JSON mismatch as reviews-load. Migrating requires a client-side card renderer with markup parity, browser-verified - out of safe scope for this static pass.

flows.name: conversation / messaging - send message (order thread)
flows.former_blocker: Pre-existing JS<->PHP contract inconsistency must be resolved before a safe migration. The AJAX send_message returns {message: 'Message sent.' (string), message_id, html (rendered)}, but conversation.js reads response.data.message as a structured object (message.id, message.attachments) and re-renders it client-side - so the current consumer/handler contract is already inconsistent. The REST twin returns prepare_message_for_response (a structured object), which actually matches the JS consumer's expectation, but switching to it changes the response shape vs the (inconsistent) AJAX shape and must be browser-verified on a live thread (text + image attachment) before shipping. Per the stability mandate (never fix blindly; browser-verify every messaging flow), deferred from this static pass.

flows.name: profile update incl. intro video (flow #12)
flows.former_blocker: The REST twin is NOT a faithful twin. (1) Field coverage diverges: the AJAX handler writes tagline, bio, country, city, website, intro_video_url (validated via wpss_is_supported_video_url), vacation_mode, vacation_message, avatar_id, cover_image_id; VendorsController::update_current_vendor handles only bio, tagline, skills, languages, social_links, avatar_id, response_time, display_name - it does NOT handle intro_video_url (the flow #12 field), country, city, website, vacation_*, or cover. (2) Storage backend diverges: AJAX writes to the {prefix}wpss_vendor_profiles custom table; the REST twin writes to user_meta. Migrating as-is would silently DROP the intro video + several profile fields and split storage - a guaranteed data-loss regression that violates 'byte-compatible; nothing removed'. A correct migration requires bringing update_current_vendor to full field + custom-table parity AND a profile read/write round-trip browser-verified for the intro-video embed - a larger piece of work than a static JS swap.

resolved_gaps: KG-1: single-service.js reviews load-more now GETs /wpss/v1/reviews and renders each item client-side via renderReviewItem() with markup parity; ReviewsController gained additive presentation fields (created_human, review_html, vendor_reply_html/_human). Browser-verified on service 16 (198 reviews).
KG-2: review 'helpful' now POSTs /wpss/v1/reviews/{id}/helpful, reads {count}. Verified with KG-1 as one unit.

KG-3: services grid now GETs /wpss/v1/services/grid (server-rendered cards+pagination via shared wpss_render_services_grid; the service-card template + its extension hooks preserved). Fixed a REST-context fatal in wpss_pagination (get_pagenum_link guard + explicit base). Verified page 2 of 30.

KG-4: order + dashboard messaging migrated to REST (POST /orders/{id}/conversation/messages creates-on-first-send + multipart attachments; poll via GET /conversations/{id}/messages?after_id=). Shared wpss_render_message_row + wpss_handle_message_attachments. Dead conversation.js removed. Browser-verified text + image + live poll on order 49 / conversation 9.

KG-5: vendor-profile now writes ONE canonical store (wpss_vendor_profiles) via VendorService::update_profile() for both REST PUT /vendors/me and the legacy AJAX; intro_video_url/country/city/website/vacation/cover all persist. Also fixed the vendor guard (wpss_is_vendor() vs raw _wpss_is_vendor meta) that rejected role-based vendors on both transports. Browser-verified: PUT 200, DB persisted, read-back, intro-video embed renders.
KG-6: the live single-service favorite (.wpss-fav-toggle) was already REST via frontend.js; the dead .wpss-favorite-btn handler in single-service.js was removed. apiUrl+restNonce localized.

KG-7: delivery submission now POSTs /orders/{id}/deliverables with multipart files[] (create_deliverable ingests raw $_FILES via shared wpss_normalize_uploaded_files; the prior integer-ID files arg never actually attached files). Browser-verified on order 49: 201, attachment stored, order -> pending_approval.
